items.title: The Fock-space convention dictionary for finite type-A quantum modules
items.statement: Use source parameter $s$ and library parameter $t=s^{-1}$. For every finite interval $[k,r]\subset I^+$ choose the type-A root datum with full $gl$ coordinate weight lattice, including its central torus. The source generators have $D_av_b=s^{\delta_{ab}}v_b$, $E_av_b=\delta_{a+1,b}v_a$, $F_av_b=\delta_{a,b}v_{a+1}$ and coproduct $\Delta E_a=1\otimes E_a+E_a\otimes D_aD_{a+1}^{-1}$, $\Delta F_a=F_a\otimes1+D_a^{-1}D_{a+1}\otimes F_a$. The semilinear Hopf dictionary sends library $E_a,F_a$ to these same divided generators and $K_h$ to $D_{-h}$; the library parameter $t$ maps to $s^{-1}$. Thus root-label weights are preserved, while toral numerical eigenvalues use the reciprocal parameter. Bar sends $s\mapsto s^{-1}$, fixes $E,F$ and inverts $D$. The natural highest weight is $\delta_k$, its dual highest weight is $-\delta_r$, and the fundamental wedge weight is $\delta_k+\cdots+\delta_m$. Every fundamental factor has its own highest-vector-normalized bar, integral lattice and divided-string crystal charts. Infinite intervals are defined by compatible finite intervals below. The SOURCE Fock $L,T,P$ families and the library form-dual upper family will be compared through their actual forms, not identified by their names.
items.strategy: Check toral actions, commutator and Serre relations generator by generator after t=s^-1 and K_h→D_-h. Both numerator and denominator of the E/F commutator change sign, so E,F are unchanged. The library coproduct E→1⊗E+E⊗K_i^-1 and F→F⊗1+K_i⊗F becomes the displayed source coproduct. Divided quantum integers are invariant under reciprocal parameter. The full coordinate lattice supplies the gl centre, so neither delta_k nor−delta_r is mislabelled as a semisimple fundamental weight. Fundamental wedges are constructed next; their internal antisymembedding is primitive integral but is not claimed lower-q0 based. Apply actual8 between these independently based fundamental factors on finite intervals; infinite-rank/tail compatibility is proved locally.

items.title: The higher-level wedge-tensor Fock module
items.statement: Fix $I$ consecutive and a positive finite level $l$, $\Lambda=\Lambda_{m_1}+\cdots+\Lambda_{m_l}\in P^+$ with $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$ (for $I$ bounded below, $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ boxes in column $j$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$; otherwise use the semi-infinite columns with common finite tails below). The **higher-level wedge-tensor Fock module** is $F(\Lambda):=V(\Lambda_{m_1})\otimes\cdots\otimes V(\Lambda_{m_l})$, the tensor product of fundamental modules of the dictionary item; when $I$ is unbounded below each $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ is the semi-infinite wedge $\Lambda^{m_j+\infty}V$ with basis the normally ordered wedges $v_{i_1}\wedge v_{i_2}\wedge\cdots$, $i_1>i_2>\cdots$, with $i_k=m_j+1-k$ for $k\gg0$. A **$\Lambda$-tableau** $A$ fills the diagram of $\Lambda$ (columns $1,\dots,l$ of heights $n_j$); it is **column-strict** if entries lie in $I^+$, strictly increase bottom to top in each column and all but finitely many entries of row $i$ equal $i$, and **standard** if in addition entries weakly increase left to right in each row. Write $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda,\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ for these sets, $A_\Lambda$ for the ground-state tableau (row $i$ filled with $i$), $M_A:=(v_{A(m_1,1)}\wedge v_{A(m_1-1,1)}\wedge\cdots)\otimes\cdots\otimes(v_{A(m_l,l)}\wedge v_{A(m_l-1,l)}\wedge\cdots)$ for the **column monomial**, $\mathrm{wt}_j(A)=\sum_{m_j\ge i\in I^+}\delta_{A(i,j)}$, $\mathrm{wt}(A)=\mathrm{wt}_1(A)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_l(A)$, and $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha=\{A:\mathrm{wt}(A)=\Lambda-\alpha\}$ for $\alpha\in Q^+$. The **Bruhat order** on $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ is $A\le B$ iff $\mathrm{wt}(A)=\mathrm{wt}(B)$ and $\mathrm{wt}_1(A)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_j(A)\ge\mathrm{wt}_1(B)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_j(B)$ in the dominance order for each $j<l$; then $A<B$ whenever $B$ is obtained from $A$ by swapping entries $a<b$ in columns $i<j$. Column-reading compositions give the passage to partitions of [[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]] and [[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]. When a column is semi-infinite, its displayed weight sum means its ground fundamental weight plus the finite sum of entry-minus-ground coordinate differences, evaluated on each finite-support coroot/torus input; no divergent infinite coordinate sum is asserted. The vector $v_\Lambda:=M_{A_\Lambda}$ is the unique monomial of weight $\Lambda$.
items.strategy: Definition only: the displayed assertions are definitions or immediate bookkeeping (bijectivity of reading down columns, one-dimensionality of the $\Lambda$-weight space of $F(\Lambda)$). The dominance/Bruhat comparison is [[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]] with [[lem-conjugation-reverses-dominance]]; no freeness or basis statement is proved here. Weight bookkeeping uses [[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]. For an unbounded interval every tableau differs from the ground state in finitely many positions; choose lower and upper finite cuts for every calculation. Finite box counts and the classical gl_n category are used only when I is bounded below.

items.title: The column monomial basis of the higher-level Fock module
items.statement: For a finite interval, normally ordered wedges $v_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge v_{i_d}$, $i_1>\cdots>i_d$, form the integral basis of the fundamental wedge, with antisymmetrizer coefficients $(-s)^{\ell(w)}$. The antisymmetrizer embedding is primitive over $\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]$; this does not assert lower-q0 basedness of that embedding into raw tensor powers. The column monomials form the tensor basis of $F(\Lambda)$, with their stated weights. Upper cuts include all entries of a given monomial; lower-cut embeddings append the common bottom $k-1$ entry to each column. Their compatible direct limit gives the full bounded or semi-infinite Fock module. All generators act by finitely many box moves and SHIFT weight spaces; fixed-weight spaces are finite-dimensional. A merely lower-bounded infinite interval need not give finite-dimensional fundamental factors; all finite-Cartan statements are applied on finite cuts.
items.strategy: Sorting the quantum exterior quotient by adjacent interchange relations gives unique ordered words: braid overlaps have the same scalar product, and repeated letters vanish. Hence the integral quotient is free, not a generic-field dimension inference. The corresponding antisymmetrizer vectors have disjoint permutation supports and ordered coefficient1, so their span is primitive/saturated. Direct E,F action replaces a valid entry once and gives0 on a repeated entry; it identifies the wedge with the fundamental highest module and its own divided-power lattice/bar/crystal. Tensoring these bases gives column monomial independence. Adding a common lower tail gives injective maps with the stated monomial action; every semi-infinite tableau belongs to some lower/upper finite cut. Fixed weight determines a finite multiset change from the common ground tail, so only finitely many tableaux occur. Direct generator formulas move finitely many boxes and are compatible once the cut contains the residue and input/output supports.

items.title: The tensor-product bar on the Fock module and its truncation compatibility
items.statement: The Fock module has the ordinary compatible bar $\psi$ fixing each ordered fundamental wedge and built by the finite-product quasi-R construction. It is involutive, independent of parenthesization, and triangular: $\psi M_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]M_B$. It preserves the integral monomial lattice. Both upper-cut embeddings and common-bottom-tail embeddings commute with this bar and preserve the actual charts/bases, so it defines a well-defined bar on the full direct limit, including semi-infinite columns. Its finite products are used only on actual finite-Cartan based fundamental factors; no universal two-sided-unbounded tensor theorem or arbitrary integral quasi-R claim is imported.
items.strategy: Use actual8 field/integral tensor-bar and crystal interfaces on finite intervals and the fundamentals' OWN based structures. Weight transfer of a positive-first quasi-R term lowers the source tableau order; the divided-power action makes its coefficients integral. Terms with a new upper endpoint>r kill the prefix, since no such entry is present and positive operators cannot create one. At a new lower endpoint k−1 every prefix wedge already contains that entry; positive operators cannot remove its smallest entry, so all new-boundary terms kill the image. Old-root terms preserve the tail. The same reasoning applies to positive-root products by looking at their first boundary generator. Thus all local operators/bars agree on the double cuts. Involution, parenthesization independence and integrality descend from actual finite8, and every vector calculation stabilizes before taking the limit. Do not confuse an internal wedge antisymembedding with a lower-chart based map.

items.title: The dual-canonical, canonical and quasi-canonical Fock bases
items.statement: Use source $s$ and the ordinary Fock bar $\psi$. The monomial basis is $M_A$. The SOURCE dual-canonical family is the $\psi$-fixed $L_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s\mathbb Z[s]M_B$; the canonical family is the $\psi$-fixed $T_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]M_B$. Define $M_B=\sum_A d_{A,B}(s)L_A$, $L_B=\sum_A p_{A,B}(-s)M_A$, and $P_A=\sum_B d_{A,B}(s)M_B$, so $M_A=\sum_Bp_{A,B}(-s)P_B$. Both $L,T$ are ordinary-bar fixed; $P$ generally is not. Reverse-factor monomials $\widetilde M_A$ and their bar/bases use reverse-column reading, with $\widetilde L_A$ supported on $B>A$. Define the SOURCE sesquilinear form by $\langle M_A,\psi M_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$ (antilinear first argument), and the bilinear reverse-factor form by $C(\widetilde M_A,\psi M_B)=\delta_{AB}$. Thus labelled monomial Gram matrices are the inverse ordinary-bar matrix, not identity. Transition duality gives $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$, $C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB}$ and $C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}$. Rectification identifies the original lower ground component $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda$ with the reverse-factor lower ground component $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$. All four families are Laurent-integral bases and commute with cuts. On the highest constituent the source bilinear normalization $C_0$ and the library polarization differ by an explicit weight power, proved in the global-basis comparison below; no unqualified library-upper/ordinary-bar identification is asserted.
items.strategy: Triangular bar correction in each finite weight set gives both complementary coefficient charts, their unitriangular inverses and integral bases; cuts preserve the same equations. If B is the ordinary-bar matrix, the defining forms have Gram B^-1. Substitute the two coefficient matrices and apply coefficient conjugation in the first sesquilinear argument to obtain the three displayed delta identities; their domains are original and reverse-factor modules as stated. Raw reverse E/F matrices are transposes of the coefficient-conjugate original F/E matrices, so the bar in the second argument gives the bilinear EF-swap contravariance with torus fixed. The sesquilinear adjoint is the source semilinear tau, not this bilinear anti-involution. Finite column signatures and row-insertion/reverse-insertion preserve the selected cancelling signs and show the two ground components and rectification dictionary; the highest-constituent theorem supplies the complete based inclusion and projection proof. Both T and L fixedness follows from their definitions and may not be contradicted later in the Definition. All of this uses the SOURCE chart normalization; actual8 upper polarization and adjoint bar are compared only after the explicit weight rescaling.

items.title: Parabolic semi-regular duality and the reverse-column label map
items.statement: For a lower-bounded Fock tableau shape, set n_j=m_j+1−inf(I), n=sum n_j and lambda_A,j=a_j+j−1 from its finite column reading. These data define the genuine finite integral parabolic CENTRAL SUMMANDS by the structural category of15; no connectedness is assumed. Assume AC. For the reversed-block standard parabolic $\bar p\subset gl_n$, grade simple Levi roots by0 and outside roots by1, so $g_0=\bar l$, $g_{<0}=\bar u^-$ and $\gamma=2\rho_g-2\rho_{\bar l}$ is a Levi character. There is the explicit semi-regular $U(g)$-bimodule $S_{\bar u,\gamma}=U(\bar u^-)^\#\otimes U(\bar p)$, with the two PBW module identifications. Tensor/Hom give inverse exact equivalences on finite-rank graded free/cofree $U(\bar u^-)$ objects. Restricted contragredient dual and $c(X)=-w_0X^tw_0$ give an exact CONTRAVARIANT equivalence $\Psi$ from finite generalized-standard flags for $\bar p$ to those for $p$. The Levi highest-weight map is $\lambda_{\bar A}\mapsto-w_{\bar J}\lambda_{\bar A}-2\rho_{\bar u}$, then $-w_0$; in reverse/original column readings it gives $a_i+i-1$, so $\Psi(\bar\Delta(A))\cong\Delta(A)$. BGG restricted duality $D$ gives the COVARIANT equivalence $F=D\Psi$ from opposite standard flags to target costandard flags, with $F(\bar\Delta(A))=\nabla(A)$. It preserves the corresponding central blocks and reverses the label order. These are exact filtered-category assertions, not equivalences on all objects of category O and not the unchanged underived full-longest Borel twisting functor.
items.strategy: Highest-weight/Levi admissibility and shifted-multiset character follow directly from these readings and the actual15 generic category, independently of the later connected-block Definition. Use the outside-root grading and finite-Levi PBW slices from15. The character identity gamma([X,Y])=tr_l(adX adY) follows by Levi invariance, checking outside simple e_alpha against f_alpha with the root/sl2 trace calculation; other weights give0. Construct right action via N# tensor_N U and left action via Hom_B(U,C_gamma tensor B). For H in l, H(f tensor1)=−(f adH)tensor1+f tensor(H+gamma(H)); for X in g1 decompose nX=Xn+sum H_i H_i^X(n)+F_X(n), giving X(f tensor1)=f tensorX+sum(fH_i^X)tensor(H_i+gamma(H_i))+(fF_X)tensor1. Commutation with right g−1 reduces to the displayed trace identity, and generation by g0,g±1 proves bimodule commutation. The left PBW map is triangular for positive Levi-radical degree followed by Levi PBW degree: leading f tensor b and strictly lower corrections prove surjectivity and injectivity by finite induction, avoiding the source's false finite-dimensional degree-zero comparison. The adjoint unit/counit reduce to graded free/cofree evaluation and End_N(N#)=N^op, so no completion is hidden. On an induced finite Levi simple E, the dual top space is C_−gamma tensor E*, hence the stated standard transport; induction restricts both functors to finite flags. Ungraded transfer uses zeta eigenvalue classes moduloZ and restricted weight duals. In a target column of lengthr and offsetb the reverse source offset isb'=n−b−r; w0w_Jbar preserves within-column position and 2w0rho_ubar=b−b'. Thus transformed component a_i+(b'+k−1)+(b−b')=a_i+i−1. This proves the exact label and scalar central shift. D then changes variance and standards to costandards. The source free/cofree and flag hypotheses are checked here, not presumed for arbitrary O.

items.title: Standard- and costandard-filtered objects and tilting objects
items.statement:
Assume the inherited AC for the finite genuine parabolic CENTRAL SUMMANDS and their highest-weight ideals; no connectedness is assumed. $\mathcal F(\Delta)$ and $\mathcal F(
abla)$ denote finite standard/costandard flags; a tilting object has both. These exact categories are closed under sums and summands, multiplicities are independent, $\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_A,
abla_B)=\delta_{AB}\mathbb C$ and all positive Ext vanish. The finite highest-weight criteria are $\mathcal F(\Delta)=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^1(N,
abla_A)=0\  orall A\}$ and its dual, equivalently using all positive Ext. Restricted duality exchanges the two flags. The normalized indecomposable tilting of label A has $\Delta_A$ once at the bottom and all other standard labels STRICTLY SMALLER in the tableau order; A is the unique maximal support label, not a minimal one. In a lower ideal containing A this tilting is unchanged.
items.strategy: Consume the ACTUAL generalized-standard trace/Hom/Ext1/BGG proof of15, not the ordinary Verma lemma restricted without proof. Standard projective kernels and dual injective cokernels have flags with strictly ordered support; dimension shifting gives higher Ext vanishing. For the homological criterion, Ext1(N,∇)=0 gives all higher Ext by those finite costandard coresolutions. Remove a maximal label e from the basic finite block algebra; the canonical trace gives heredity ideal Ae⊗eA with Ae=Δ_e,eAe=C. For B=A/AeA every injective B-object is costandard-filtered with the lower labels, so all positive Ext_A(N,I_B) vanish. A projective resolution and tensor/Hom adjunction then force Tor_j^A(B,N)=0 (injective B-objects detect its homology). Hence 0→Ae⊗eN→N→B⊗N→0; the quotient has the same vanishing overB and induction gives a standard flag. Duality proves the other criterion. Idempotent trace peeling preserves flags under summands. The tilting classification theorem applies these criteria and proves the maximal-label uniqueness; no false Δ→∇ injection or min-label hypothesis is used.

items.title: Type-A tableau central summands are single linkage blocks
items.statement: Assume AC. For the Fock shape $n_1\ge\cdots\ge n_l$ (the original nonincreasing-charge hypothesis) and any admitted integral entry multiset, the genuine $gl_n$ parabolic central summand labelled by its strict-column tableaux is a SINGLE linkage block. The same holds for its reverse-column/reversed-Levi counterpart. This includes repeated-entry singular ambient characters. The proof uses actual indecomposable generalized standards and locally constructed tiltings: adjacent-column positive exclusive-pair canonical coefficients specialize to1, so those labels lie in a common actual linkage block; these edges connect the whole fixed-margin binary tableau fiber. No future higher-Schur/cyclotomic-centre theorem is imported.
items.strategy: Do not presume connectedness. Work in the actual15 finite highest-weight central summand, possibly a product, and use the earlier parabolic standard-flag equivalence Psi. Put X(B)=Psi(Pbar(B)). Its standard flag has labelB once at the bottom and onlyA<B otherwise, by opposite BGG/order reversal. Projectivity makes Ext1(Delta,X)=0, so the independently proved generic criterion makes X tilting. Both X andDX have the same maximal normalized flag; extending the bottom inclusion both ways and finite local-End/Fitting proves selfduality. Thus (X(B):M(A))=[barM(A):barL(B)]. To identify these coefficients with SOURCE T at1, use the direct tensor/wedge matrix bridge: sortingw is shortestRIGHT in the ENTRY stabilizer and d=w^-1 shortestLEFT. Pure tensor Hecke generator action and the reverse-position complementary-chart pairing (sourceB1§4, with reciprocal parameter) identify tensor d(1) with spherical P_{d(C)w0,d(A)w0}(1), exactly15singular ordinary multiplicities. Finite Levi Weyl cancellation gives the signed column-permutation expansion of genuine generalized standards. Source-positive wedge embedding sends its L to tensorL by ordinary-bar and triangular uniqueness, hence the same signed matrix is the actual parabolic d. Apply this also in reverse columns. The typed C(tildeL,T)=delta gives (X(B):M(A)) equal to the coefficient of M(A) in source T_B at1. All this concerns central SUMMANDS, so invokes neither connectedDefinition nor later16Ringel/tilting theorem. Now independently construct the two-column canonical coefficient: CWZ0409016§4.3–4.4 defines disjoint positive pairs (left exclusive b>right exclusive a), chosen by increasing b−a distance and discarding previously used endpoints. With q=t=s^-1 its normal wedge action/coproduct equals this library/source dictionary. The source3case Procedure4.11 reduces to a typical tuple with no positive pairs; its monomial is ordinary-bar fixed since every positive-first quasi-R correction would need an exclusive b>a pair. In the reduction steps the explicit wedge Chevalley formulas give either K_f alone or K_f+qK_swapped. Each Chevalley generator is bar fixed. The recursion terminates lexicographically in the number of matched pairs and the sum of their distances: losing a pair lowers the first measure, and retaining the pairs moves only the selected endpoint inward. The source Lem4.14 induction therefore gives a bar-fixed qZ[q]-triangular vector; uniqueness identifies the canonical vector. Its3cases prove U_f=sum_{Sigma subset greedy positivepairs}q^{#Sigma}K_{fSigma}. Distinct subsets change distinct exclusive entries, so each single-pair coefficient is EXACTLYq. This is a complete two-factor proof, not a super-duality conjecture. For adjacent columns in a larger tensor, endpoints agreeing outside those columns have identical outer prefix weights. Every tableau in their Bruhat interval has those same outer prefix weights. Parenthesize with the pair as one factor: a positive transfer across an outer boundary would strictly change a prefix weight and cannot be cancelled by further positive transfers. Thus the interval bar matrix, and by triangular correction its canonical coefficient, equals the two-column matrix. At1 a greedy-pair edge gives (X(B):M(A))=1; indecomposable X(B) has both simple heads as composition factors, so A,B lie in the SAME actual original block. Opposite BGG gives [barM(A):barL(B)]=1, and barM(A) also has headbarL(A), so the same edge connects the opposite blocks. To connect all labels, identify a tableau with the0/1 incidence matrix of which entry values occur in each column; row margins are entry multiplicities and column margins are n_j. Two such matrices differ by alternating cycles in their bipartite symmetric difference. A long cycle splits by a chord: if the chord is0 flip the smaller4cycle first, otherwise flip the complementary shorter cycle first; induction flips the entire cycle while restoring the chord. Hence arbitrary valid2x2 switches connect the fiber. Reduce a switch between nonadjacent columnsS,U through the next intermediate columnT. IfT has onlya or onlyb, two switches with shorter column distance suffice. IfT contains botha,b, choose c inS\T: it exists because |S|>=|T| andT\S containsb. Perform c↔b betweenS,T, a↔b betweenT,U, thena↔c betweenS,T, restoringT and making the desired S/U switch. IfT contains neither, choosec inT\U (exists |T|>=|U| andU\T containsb), and use c↔b betweenT,U, a↔b betweenS,T, thena↔c betweenT,U. Induct distance; all switches remain binary and preserve margins. Sorted ORIGINAL heights justify precisely these cardinal comparisons. Finally any adjacent-column switch lies in a fixed two-column union/intersection fiber. Repeatedly swapping a greedy positive pair strictly lowers its inversion order until the unique configuration with all left-exclusive values below right-exclusive values; hence all such fibers connect through the already-proved coefficient1 edges. Combining the paths proves original and opposite linkage connectedness. This supplies the full promised singleblock result without merely asserting a shuffle graph or importing future17/18 centre-surjectivity.

items.statement: Assume AC and $I$ bounded below, so $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are finite (the upper end of $I$ may remain unbounded). Let classical $g=gl_n(\mathbb C)$ and the standard parabolic have Levi $gl_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus gl_{n_l}$. For the column reading $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ of $A$, set $\lambda_A=\sum_j(a_j+j-1)\varepsilon_j$ and let $L(A)$ be its simple highest module. Strict columns make this Levi-dominant, so the simple and the induced generalized standard $M(A)$ belong to genuine $O^p$. Use the published HALF-SUM convention $\rho_j=(n+1-2j)/2$. Then $\lambda_{A,j}+\rho_j=a_j+(n-1)/2$, so their $gl_n$ Harish-Chandra shifted-coordinate multiset is the tableau-entry multiset plus the common scalar $(n-1)/2$; this labels the central character, together with the displayed scalar $gl_n$ centre. The Fock weight $\sum\delta_{a_j}=\Lambda-\alpha$ belongs to the DIFFERENT $gl_{I^+}$ weight lattice and indexes that multiset, not a literal gl_n highest weight. The corresponding finite parabolic central blocks $O^\Lambda_\alpha$ have labels $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$, generalized standards $M(A)$, simples $L(A)$, projectives $P(A)$ and costandards $\nabla(A)$, with BGG and restricted duality from15. Their simple/standard bases and numerical multiplicities include repeated-entry singular central characters. The direct sum over these characters is $O^\Lambda$. Opposite blocks use reversed Levi order and reverse-column reading, with the corresponding reversed label order.
items.strategy: Finite Levi highest-weight classification applies to the derived Levi and the displayed scalar centre. PBW and the15 local-finiteness proof give the actual generalized standards; the same highest weights identify their heads and all admissible simples. The actual published Harish-Chandra supplier uses the half-sum rho, with HC_rho(z)(mu)=pr(z)(mu−rho) and central scalars evaluated at lambda+rho. For gl_n, rho_j=(n+1−2j)/2 has sum0, and lambda_j=a_j+j−1 gives lambda_j+rho_j=a_j+(n−1)/2. Thus the semisimple shifted Weyl orbit together with the trace-centre value is precisely determined by the sorted entry multiset. No undeclared full-staircase shift is used. The finite admitted parabolic labels in that integral orbit give the15 highest-weight category and character/Grothendieck bases; the preceding local linkage lemma proves SINGLE-block connectedness by actual two-column canonical coefficient1/indecomposable tilting edges and a complete fixed-margin switch argument, including saturated/common rows. This is the specific type-A result, not a generic consequence of a central-character decomposition. Reverse-column reading swaps Levi blocks and reverses prefix order, as computed in the semiregular label helper. No identification with projectively parabolic-presentable properly stratified objects is made.

items.title: Parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials give the dual-canonical transition matrix
items.statement:
For $I$ bounded below use the actual finite classical tableau-block dictionary (including repeated entries). Fix the right place action $(a w)_i=a_{w(i)}$. Let $w_A$ be shortest with $a(A)w_A$ weakly increasing, and let $K$ be the Young stabilizer of that sorted multiset. Then $w_A$ is shortest RIGHT modulo $K$, $d(A)=w_A^{-1}$ shortest LEFT, and
$$p_{A,B}(s)=s^{\ell(w_B)-\ell(w_A)}\sum_{z\in K}(-1)^{\ell(z)}P_{w_Az,w_B}(s^{-2}).$$
This is the ANTISPHERICAL/sign family for the ENTRY stabilizer, in the left convention after inversion, with Hecke variable $v=s$; the library QUANTUM parameter is instead $t=s^{-1}$. It has support $A\le B$ and diagonal1; $d$ is its inverse coefficient matrix through $p(-s)$. The COLUMN Levi subgroup $J$ is generally different from $K$. Assuming AC, the genuine parabolic block composition matrix is
$$[M(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)=\sum_{C\sim_{\rm col}B}(-1)^{\ell(B,C)}P_{d(C)w_0,d(A)w_0}(1).$$
This uses singular ordinary SPHERICAL coefficients for the entry stabilizer inside finite Levi cancellation, so covers mixed singular-ambient/parabolic-Levi blocks. It does not identify a singular category with genuine parabolic O or identify the two polynomial families by an opposite convention.
items.strategy: Check the tensor Hecke generators directly on tuple monomials, with reciprocal sourceB1 parameter; sorting identifies trivial induction for K and the opposite triangular chart is sign induction. Project ordinary KL vectors to the sign quotient. Simultaneous inversion gives p_{w_Az,w_B}=p_{z^-1d(A),d(B)}, so the15 alternating-sum/triangular uniqueness theorem gives the displayed FULL polynomial identity, not a sample or q=1 family test. The source-positive-s wedge antisymembedding has ordered leading coefficient1, positive-degree within-column corrections and compatible ordinary bar (highest-factor intertwining and quasi-R naturality). Expanding a source L_A gives the ambient tensor L_{a(A)} by positive-chart uniqueness; this embedding is not asserted library-lower based. At1,15 singular ordinary multiplicities give [M(a):L(c)]=P_{w_a w0,w_cw0}(1)=P_{d(a)w0,d(c)w0}(1), by inversion plus longest conjugation. Finite Levi Weyl characters/PBW give ch M(B)=sum_C (−1)^ell(B,C)ch ordinaryM(C). Comparing with the same signed exterior monomial expansion in the tensor L basis proves d_AB(1) equals the displayed mixed parabolic matrix, using character injectivity. Thus regular and singular ambient cases are both closed locally without Koszul or double-coset category equivalence.

items.title: Standard tableau monomials form a basis of the highest weight Fock submodule
items.statement: The highest vector $M_{A_\Lambda}$ generates the multiplicity-one constituent $V(\Lambda)\subset F(\Lambda)$ and there is its normalized module projection $\pi$. The vectors $S_A=\pi M_A$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, form a basis, and $D_A=\pi L_A$ on that set form the SOURCE dual-canonical basis. What vanishes is $\pi L_A$ for $A$ not standard; $\pi M_A$ need not vanish there. The integral kernel is the saturated direct summand with basis $L_A$ off $\mathrm{Std}$, and $\pi(F_\mathcal A)$ has the actual basis $D_A$ (also $S_A$ on $\mathrm{Std}$), the source upper/costandard lattice. For every $B$, $\pi M_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}}d_{A,B}(s)D_A$, giving explicit straightening of nonstandard projected monomials. All bases/maps commute with upper cuts and common-tail embeddings; this proves the full direct-limit assertion. The relation of source $D_A$ to the library form-dual upper family is the weight rescaling below, not an unqualified identification.
items.strategy: Use a based HIGHEST inclusion, not an internal antisymembedding. The map j:VΛ→F sends the pure ground highest monomial, maps the divided-power lattice into F_A, commutes intrinsic lower divided-string operators and sends their zero chart into the actual finite8 tensor chart. Every crystal edge remains nonzero by partial inverses. It commutes ordinary bar by equality on the highest generator, hence maps the infinity chart too; balanced uniqueness gives jG_low=T on the original lower ground component Rev. For the reverse-factor product the same proof gives tildeT on Std. The column signature rule cancels−+ and selects rightmost+/leftmost−; neighbor row inequalities prove Std closed. At a highest tableau the rightmost column is consecutive ground; inductively overlapping rows force ground in earlier columns, and a gap above the overlap has an unmatched−. Raising terminates by bounded entry sum, so Std is exactly that component. Reverse column order with the prescribed top slides gives Rev; row/reverse insertion is a crystal isomorphism because the two elementary Knuth moves preserve cancelling signs and follow the changed entry along its bump path. This proves both actual label sets. Define π by C0(v,πy)=C(j_reverse v,y), where C0 is the normalized nondegenerate EF-swap form on the highest constituents. The typed contravariance of C gives U-linearity and highest normalization identifies the canonical projection. C(tildeT_A,L_B)=δ then proves vanishing offStd and gives D_Std as the C0-dual basis. Restricting the unitriangular d matrix to Std makes S_Std a basis and gives the explicit straightening inverse. The integral kernel/images follow from this actual basis, not from an A-unit Gram determinant. Finite double-cut compatibility and unique highest maps give the full limit proof. No quantum flag algebra, PeterWeyl or category-O dimension argument is imported.

items.title: The residue translation functors on the sum of parabolic blocks
items.statement: Assume AC and finite classical $gl_n$ tableau blocks. Define $f_i$ by tensoring with its natural module and projecting onto the entry-multiset character with one $i$ replaced by $i+1$; define $e_i$ by the dual natural module and the reverse character change. On their direct sum these are exact and biadjoint, preserve projectives/injectives and commute with the restricted transpose duality. Equivalently $f_i$ is the generalized eigencomponent $i$ of tensor Casimir and $e_i$ is the generalized eigencomponent $-n-i$ on the dual tensor product. They are special residue translations, not automatically ordinary regular-wall translations. The Fock root label shifts by $\pm\alpha_i$; that label is not the classical gl_n highest weight.
items.strategy: General finite-tensor/block-projection biadjunction is the ACTUAL general clause of the published translation supplier, applied to V and V*, not a sequence of unproved regular wall crossings. Tensor finite modules preserves genuine parabolic local finiteness, and exact block projection/Levi Hom gives the same adjunction inside O^p. Restricted transpose duality fixes both finite natural modules with their respective forms, so each residue functor commutes with it. Highest-weight scalar Casimir calculation is supplied by the earlier local Casimir lemma before any head/socle consumer. All block labels are the explicit shifted-coordinate multisets.

items.title: Residue Casimir operators and local affine-Hecke actions
items.statement: Assume AC and work with finite $n$ classical $gl_n$ category O, distinct from the Fock algebra $gl_{I^+}$. Tensor Casimir $x_j$ on the jth natural factor (including all preceding factors) and adjacent place swaps $T_j$ on $M\otimes V^{\otimes r}$ satisfy the degenerate affine-Hecke relations: commuting $x_j$, symmetric-group braid/quadratic relations, $T_jx_j-x_{j+1}T_j=-1$ and commuting distant generators. They restrict naturally to repeated residue functors $f_i^r$, where $x_j-i$ is locally nilpotent; dual actions are biadjoint mates on $e_i^r$. Finite Levi tensor decomposition and exact PBW induction give multiplicity-free generalized-standard flags for the entry moves $i\to i+1$ and $i+1\to i$. The standard-class map $[\Delta(A)]\mapsto M_A$ gives the full integral Fock K0 action, its Chevalley/Serre relations and local integrability; each root's biadjoint functors therefore give a positive, locally finite $sl_2$ action on the simple-class basis. The ground-state class generates the highest constituent, not generally the entire tensor Fock module.
items.strategy: The natural tensor Casimir is sum E_ab tensor E_ba, and x_j adds the place transpositions with earlier natural factors. Matrix-unit multiplication proves x commutation and T_jx_jT_j=x_{j+1}−T_j, hence the listed relations, with braid and distant commutation immediate on places. For highest weight lambda_j=a_j+j−1, c(lambda)=sum lambda_j(lambda_j+n+1−2j), c(V)=n; the eigenvalue on the lambda+epsilon_j flag factor is (c(lambda+epsilon_j)−c(lambda)−n)/2=lambda_j+1−j=a_j. On lambda−epsilon_j in tensor V* it is −a_j−n+1; an entry i+1 therefore gives −n−i. Exact generalized eigenspaces select precisely the moves. Tensor identity plus finite Levi complete reducibility produces each valid column move once; projected invalid/repeated-column moves disappear. Standard and simple K0 bases and character injectivity were proved in15, so the standard-class map is an actual isomorphism and the induced generators are the explicit tensor/wedge action. Checking on this basis proves Chevalley and Serre relations, including the integral divided powers. Each residue root is locally finite because the fixed finite boxes have only two relevant entries and repeated replacements terminate. Biadjunction, finite length and positivity in the simple basis make class vanishing equivalent to functor vanishing, satisfying every weak-sl2 hypothesis without a forward reference to the later combined action theorem. Restrict x to the chosen generalized eigenfunctor; nilpotence follows on finite flags, hence on finite length. Define the dual x/T by mates, which preserves the relations and both adjunctions.

items.title: The local affine-Hecke socle argument for residue translations
items.statement: Assume AC and the preceding positive biadjoint residue $sl_2$/local degenerate affine-Hecke action. At a coincident eigenvalue the completed affine-Hecke algebra on r steps is $Mat_{r!}$ over the completed symmetric polynomial centre. The first-i image in its central fibre is $Mat_{i!}(Z_{i,r})$, where $Z_{i,r}=\mathbb C[c_1,\ldots,c_i]/(h_{r-i+1},\ldots,h_r)$ is a finite local complete-intersection Frobenius ring of dimension $\binom ri$ and one-dimensional socle. Divided residue functors and the complementary-idempotent restriction have the corresponding simple head/socle. Consequently $e_iL(A)$ and $f_iL(A)$ are either0 or self-dual indecomposables with simple isomorphic head and socle labelled $\tilde e_iA$ and $\tilde f_iA$, respectively. Vanishing is exactly absence of that crystal edge. This retains the complete residue-translation crystal claim, not only its K0 action.
items.strategy: Use polynomial representation T_j=s_j−partial_j, partial_j=(1−s_j)/(x_j−x_{j+1}); PBW follows by ordered spanning and leading permutation independence after localization. At the coincident completion, partial_j=(x_j−x_{j+1}+1)^−1(1−T_j), with LEFT inverse. Polynomial multiplication and longest divided difference give the relative perfect trace; reduction is the actual coinvariant Frobenius pairing, and complete-local Nakayama gives every matrix unit. The trivial/sign symmetric-group idempotents have fibre rank1: divided-difference terms lower degree and the diagonal character is the regular coinvariant character; idempotent splitting and Nakayama lift rank1. Partial elimination of remaining elementary coefficients gives the displayed h-relations. Their only common zero is0, since vanishing of i consecutive h's and their recurrence makes the reciprocal elementary series polynomial, hence constant. Nullstellensatz makes the quotient finite; polynomial Cohen–Macaulayness and the actual system-of-parameters theorem give regularity, globally by homogeneous localization. Koszul Hilbert series yields dimension binomial(r,i); the variable and h Koszul resolutions compute a unique socle in degree i(r−i). Thus no Grassmannian/Poincare theorem is imported. The ordered partial ring is free of rank i! over this centre and has dimension r!/(r−i)!, by successive monic distinguished-root equations. PBW group cosets and this basis prove the restriction freeness; the complementary idempotent removes (r−i)! multiplicity and leaves the indecomposable projective over Mat_{i!}(Z), with simple head/socle. These are the full algebraic steps of CR3.2–3.3/3.6. In the positive simple-class basis the sl2 string-height filtration is stable; biadjunction prevents a socle/head summand of E^jS from having lower maximal string height than S. At an extremal simple FS=0, E^(r)S is a single opposite-extremal simple by finite sl2 string theory/positivity. The Hecke action on E^rS has multiplicity module K_r; complementary restriction forces the socle/head of E^(j)S simple, since no maximal-height summand is killed by E^(r−j). Dimension comparison gives binomial(r,j) leading multiplicity and smaller-height other factors. For a general S take an extremal quotient of F^(h_minus)S and use adjunction to embed S in its divided translate; the opposite extremal translate is a sum of one simple, and the adjoint Hom into its simple socle bounds its multiplicity by1. This proves CR5.20 without importing it as a black box. Source Fock L is the balanced SOURCE upper-chart family. Kashiwara93§5.1 proves kernels of powers spanned by the global vectors with bounded epsilon (apply the maximal string power and balanced injectivity); §5.2 finite sl2 highest-string filtration is balanced by isolating a maximal constituent and annihilator test, whose remainder lies in the zero triple intersection. Thus in each associated string fG=[phi]G(tilde f) and eG=[epsilon]G(tilde e), and all other constituents have smaller corresponding height. The actual upper/lower string definitions in§3, the two source-positive coefficient charts and the typed reverse pairing verify these hypotheses; this is not the library8 adjoint-bar family by fiat. The full source5.3.1 proof uses the upper divided-string expansion and kernel-spanning induction to lift that leading term. At1, comparing with the preceding categorical unique maximal-height factors gives precisely the stated tableau labels. Commuting restricted duality makes head and socle equal and gives self-duality; one simple socle forces indecomposability.

items.title: The residue translation functors give the integrable Fock-space action
items.statement: Assume AC. The exact residue functors on genuine finite-n parabolic blocks have multiplicity-free generalized-standard flags given by valid single-entry moves $i\to i+1$ and $i+1\to i$. Their K0 operators are the full integrable $gl_{I^+}$ Fock Chevalley action, satisfying the integral Chevalley/Serre relations on the standard basis. The full tensor Fock module is represented by all standard classes; the ground-state class, with $M(A_\Lambda)=L(A_\Lambda)=P(A_\Lambda)$, generates only its multiplicity-one highest constituent. No action on labels alone proves the K0 relations or head/socle statement.

Apply it with E=f_i,F=e_i (and the swapped root orientation), then use restricted duality. For the ground multiset the column-strict admitted label is unique: successive strict entries at least their row ground values, with that minimal total weight forcing equality. The15 highest-weight/character bases therefore make its standard simple and projective. items.title: The parabolic category-O Grothendieck group is the integral Fock module
items.statement: Assume AC and $I$ bounded below. The standard-class map $[M(A)]\mapsto M_A$ identifies the direct-sum K0 of genuine tableau parabolic blocks with the full integral Fock module, with matching multiset degrees and residue Chevalley action of $gl_{I^+}$. For every projective $P$ and finite-length $N$, $\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)=\langle[P],[N]\rangle$ at $s=1$. In particular $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$; no false standard/simple orthogonality $\langle M_A,L_B\rangle=\delta$ is asserted. The projective, simple and tilting basis identifications are proved separately below.
items.strategy: Use the genuine15 finite-length simple/standard bases and the earlier Casimir standard-flag operator identification. Character injectivity makes the displayed map an isomorphism in each finite block, then direct sums preserve it. The mixed multiplicity theorem gives the actual standard/simple transition matrix. items.title: Indecomposable tilting objects exist and are classified in parabolic category O
items.statement: Assume AC. Every label A in a genuine tableau parabolic block has a unique indecomposable tilting $T(A)$ whose standard flag begins with $M(A)$ once at the bottom and all remaining labels $B<A$. Equivalently it has that maximal-label normalized standard flag and $\operatorname{Ext}^1(M(B),T(A))=0$ for all B. Every tilting is a finite direct sum of these and their classes form a unitriangular Grothendieck basis. Restricted duality fixes $T(A)$. For a finite lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing A the corresponding partial tilting is the SAME ambient $T(A)$, since all support is $\le A$; compatible ideal systems therefore stabilize in each finite block, with the stated flag-preserving inclusions. No uniqueness is claimed from a bottom-standard occurrence alone without indecomposability/maximal support. In the original inline prinjectivity claim, P(A) is projective-injective (equivalently self-dual) exactly when A is standard; in that case P(A)=T(A^up) with the proved rectification label.
items.strategy: Apply the independently proved parabolic semiregular CONTRAVARIANT standard-flag equivalence to opposite projective Pbar(A). Extensions from target standards to its image invert to split extensions of the opposite projective, so Ext1(Δ,−)=0 and the preceding genuine finite-highest-weight criterion makes it tilting. Opposite BGG/reversed order gives labelA once with onlyB<A, and maximal trace arranges Δ_A at the bottom. For two candidates, extend the common bottom inclusion both ways using Ext1 against standard flags; composites restrict to its identity, hence are nonnilpotent. Finite-dimensional local End/Fitting forces isomorphisms. For any tilting summand choose a maximal flag label, extend maps to/from its T(A), split the resulting idempotent and induct on length. Duality preserves its normalized support so fixes it by uniqueness. This also proves partial-ideal and Grothendieck basis assertions. No Irving prinjectivity criterion or Borel-only theorem is imported. The inline prinjectivity proof is also local. The full source-positive projection kernel spanned by L_offStd is U-stable, and the actual mixed multiplicity map identifies these with simple classes. Since residue functors have nonnegative composition coefficients, iterating them on an offStd simple never gives a Std composition factor. Every generalized standard M(B) embeds into an iterated e-word of an irreducible standard M(C): add successively huge offsets to the later columns so all later entries lie above earlier ones, making C the unique minimum in its fixed-multiset tableau order, hence its standard is simple. Lower the later-column entries back, columns left-to-right and entries bottom-to-top, with the explicit residue word. A later column remains above the active residues; a wrong move can only occur in an earlier column and strictly increases an earlier prefix weight, so the intended B is the unique maximal final standard section and occurs once. Exact flags and the canonical maximal trace embed M(B) at the bottom. Use a temporary larger finite alphabet for this finite word, returning to the original character. If L(A) embeds M(B), adjunction gives the Std L(C) as a quotient of an f-word on L(A), impossible offStd by kernel stability/positivity. Conversely each Std label is reached from the unique ground simple projective by the crystal f-word. The proved simple-head clause makes P(A) a summand of that translated projective-injective, hence injective. A projective-injective indecomposable is self-dual: DP(A)=P(B), the simple classes are duality-fixed, and the Cartan matrix is D D^transpose with unitriangular D, hence invertible; [P(A)]=[P(B)] forces A=B. SelfdualP(A) has its head in its socle and its standard flag embeds that simple into a standard section. Finally P_Std=s^a T_Aup in the proved pure highest normalization gives equality of classes at1; since P(A) is an indecomposable tilting, its unique maximal standard label identifies it as T(A^up). No Irving or futureSchur theorem is imported.

items.title: The Ringel dual of a finite highest weight ideal
items.statement: Assume AC. In a finite highest-weight block or lower Serre ideal $\Gamma$, put $T_\Gamma=\bigoplus_{A\in\Gamma}T(A)$ and $R_\Gamma=\operatorname{End}(T_\Gamma)^{op}$. This is a characteristic tilting generator, Ext-self-orthogonal with finite projective dimension. Its Ringel-dual category is highest weight with the REVERSED poset and standards $\Delta_R(A)=\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,\nabla(A))$. The Hom functor is exact and fully faithful on costandard-filtered objects and identifies them with STANDARD-filtered Ringel-dual objects; projectives of the dual correspond to tiltings of the original. Its algebraic realization by the opposite-parabolic highest-weight quotient is proved next.
items.strategy: The preceding finite criteria give higher Ext(T,∇)=0 and finite standard/projective resolutions, hence finite projective dimension and Ext-self-orthogonality for T. Dual to Δ_A→T(A), every costandard has a tilting epimorphism with costandard-filtered kernel; induction gives such presentations for every costandard-flag object. Hom(T,−) is exact on these flags and sends tiltings to projectives. Two tilting presentations lift every map and identify its kernel, proving full faithfulness and giving the reverse construction for successive Δ_R extensions. The quotient Hom(T,T(A))→Hom(T,∇A) has a standard-flag kernel with labels strictly higher in the reversed order; EndΔ_R=C and head labelA follow from the actual full-faithful Hom and maximal tilting support. Thus the Ringel category is highest weight and its filtered image is F(Δ_R), not F(∇_R). In a lower ideal its characteristic tiltings are the unchanged ambient ones by support, so this proof applies to each finite ideal.

Therefore the full-block Ringel dual is the opposite-parabolic block, and $(T(A):M(B))=[\bar M(B):\bar L(A)]$. For a proper original lower ideal $\Gamma$, its Ringel dual is the matching opposite HIGHEST-WEIGHT SERRE QUOTIENT by the complementary labels (an upper ideal in the opposite order), not the same Serre down-set subcategory. items.title: The canonical and quasi-canonical bases need not coincide
items.statement: In $I=\{0\}$, $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$, $P_{01}=M_{01}+sM_{10}=sT_{10}$, but $P_{10}=M_{10}$ while $T_{10}=M_{10}+s^{-1}M_{01}$. Hence the canonical and quasi-canonical families are different over $\mathbb Q(s)$; so are the dual-canonical and monomial families. The highest-component label rectification is $01^\uparrow=10$ and $a=1$, proving the genuine power/label distinction. At $s=1$ the highest-submodule vectors $P_{01}$ and $T_{10}$ agree after rectification, but the full canonical and quasi-canonical families are still not interchangeable. This is no claim that every corresponding label differs at1.
